answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to forge its standing through a long, verifiable history of useful work: every completed task leaves a signed, non-transferable record, like stones building a river bed, so reputation accumulates slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. A newcomer sends only a weak trust signal until its record deepens, while creating thousands of fake identities would mean redoing that costly history for each one, making an attack far more expensive than any gain from flooding the network.
